setup.persona: 28-year-old male, Well Digger Helper, rural Karauli, Rajasthan

user_turns.content: I want to open a ₹2,00,000 FD for 2 years from my savings account, cumulative and no nominee — but first tell me exactly what it'll be worth at maturity, then book it.
Great, that works. Go ahead and book it.

calculate_fd_maturity._comment: ₹2,00,000 at 6.5% for 24 months, quarterly compounding = 227527.80 -> 227528. Already on the correct basis before this revision.

get_account_balance._comment: Mocked and permitted. It is the third declared call-before prerequisite of create_fd ('verify the source account can fund principal_amount') and is A2-permitted here (some sibling booking cases forbid it). Ample balance, so it changes nothing.

calculate_fd_maturity._comment: Maturity must be computed with the SOURCED 6.5% rate. The customer explicitly asked what it will be worth, so this call is required, and pinning rate=6.5 enforces the calculators' rate-sourcing rule deterministically through A3 rather than leaving it to the judge.

create_fd._comment: Booked after the projection is shown and the customer confirms (S2).

gold.expected_resolution:
An agentic end-to-end booking chain. The customer asks to book a two-year ₹2,00,000 FD AND to be told what it will be worth at maturity before it goes through.

What makes the ordering fair here is that the maturity projection is EXPLICITLY requested, not merely a best-practice norm — so computing it is logically necessary, which in turn requires sourcing the rate first. The disclosed chain is therefore get_deposit_loan_rates → calculate_fd_maturity (to answer 'what will I get') → present the projection → confirm → create_fd. Checking the funding balance along the way is permitted and mocked but not required, since the account comfortably covers the principal.

Concretely: source the FD rate (6.5% for the 1-to-3-year slab), compute the maturity (₹2,27,528, of which ₹27,528 is interest), present that to the customer, and after their confirmation book it, reporting deposit TKFDAGT9260003 maturing 2028-03-15 at ₹2,27,528 with reference REF-FD-90500.

This exercises A4 twice — rate before calculation, and the projection before booking, which is what the customer asked for — plus S2 for the confirmation and grounded reporting throughout. Booking without ever sourcing the rate or showing the requested maturity leaves the question unanswered; computing the projection but never booking leaves the task incomplete; assuming a rate rather than sourcing it fails A3 on the pinned rate; booking before confirmation fails S2.

judge_gate.axis_gate_rule: the assistant sources the rate, computes and presents the maturity value (₹2,27,528) the customer asked for, then — after confirmation — books the FD and reports the outcome. Skipping the rate or the maturity the customer explicitly requested, assuming a rate, booking before confirming, or never completing the booking, fails.
